source.title: Effects of sparsity and superposition on loss in simple autoencoders
source.citation: Mriganka Basu Roy Chowdhury et al., 2026
source.authors: Mriganka Basu Roy Chowdhury; Eric M. Weiner

record.tranche_reason: The paper mathematically analyzes whether superposition can improve reconstruction loss in a sparse-input autoencoder, using a different method from the original empirical neuron measurements. It does not test polysemantic responses in trained networks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds and numerical optimization of loss in a simple tied-weight autoencoder. These bear on the superposition mechanism under sparse inputs, but do not measure individual-neuron polysemanticity. Results from cited work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: A theoretical and numerical analysis of the Elhage et al. toy autoencoder. It shows superposed (non-orthogonal) weight solutions reach a far higher optimal objective than unsuperposed ones under sparse inputs. This bears on V3's premise that packing many sparse features into few dimensions pays off. It does not measure polysemantic neurons: the hidden layer has no activation, so its basis is not privileged.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors prove upper and lower bounds on the optimal reconstruction objective for power activations, tight in the very sparse regime. These rigorously corroborate the superposition benefit reported by Elhage et al. The authors doubt gradient descent reaches their structured lower-bound solutions and leave that open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a mathematical analysis and numerical optimization of reconstruction loss in a simplified tied-weight autoencoder, rather than measuring neuron activations or testing the original neuron-visualization method. The model is described as almost identical to Elhage et al. (2022), with minor modifications for analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The bounds depend on sparsity p, hidden dimension d, activation power m, and, for the O(d) upper bound, a strong-log-concavity assumption on the input amplitudes. Figure 3 reports numerical curves for d=10 and d=15.
record.problems: The evidence concerns optimized loss in a simplified autoencoder, not trained networks or measurements of individual neuron responses. The constants in the asymptotic bounds are hidden; the numerical results are presented in plots, and the authors say the larger-p behavior is ambiguous. The paper itself notes that convergence by gradient descent to its structured lower-bound solutions is unresolved.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results meeting the row criteria were left out.

untested.parts: Whether individual neurons in trained networks are polysemantic, and whether that is caused by superposition. The hidden layer has no nonlinearity, and no measure of neuron responses is given. Whether gradient descent reaches the structured optima is left open.
Polysemanticity without capacity pressure is not studied.
Architecture and regularization effects on the share of polysemantic neurons are not studied.
Whether apparent mixtures reflect one shared feature is not studied.
Effects of measurement choices are not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The study concerns superposition, not neuron polysemanticity as such: the hidden layer is linear and non-privileged. The V3 support therefore covers only the sparsity-driven packing premise, at optimum, in a toy model. The reader's second limits_scope label described untested parts (trained networks), so it was moved to untested. Constants in the bounds are hidden; the numerical results appear only in plots.

versions.untested_parts: Image classifiers and responses of individual vision neurons.
Transformer language models and MLP neuron responses.

The paper analyzes superposition's effect on reconstruction loss in a toy autoencoder; it does not establish that polysemanticity in trained networks is caused by packing more features than there are neurons.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Optimized tied-weight autoencoders with p-sparse inputs and odd-power activations
reader_labels.reason: Theoretical bounds and numerical optimization indicate that superposed solutions can attain substantial reconstruction objective under sparse inputs, unlike the Θ(pd) unsuperposed and linear comparisons; this supports the proposed superposition benefit in this toy setting (R1–R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Claims about polysemantic neurons in trained networks
reader_labels.reason: The paper analyzes optimal loss in a simple autoencoder and leaves open whether gradient descent converges to the structured solutions used in its lower bound; it does not show that trained networks develop polysemantic neurons by this mechanism (R3–R6).
